- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags behind true price movements; increase forecast early in the horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If true price moves >2% from recent mean in 3–5 days, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast toward historical mean within 7–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to dampen overfitting.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.6 → 0.0 → 0.6), model often misreads momentum; treat as “neutral” and forecast mid-range of recent 5-day window.
